summary: Sound work buffer (base Sound_WorkBuffer): carves a caller-supplied region into 0x1B8-byte blocks for the sound library and holds two embedded SndMixState mixing states with their 0x20/0x21-entry block tables; the decoder, driver and mixer entry points all operate on this object.
evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init (0x0054B608) stores the work area and calls Snd_InitMixingState (0x00110E10) twice: (self, self+0x34, 0x20) and (self+0xB4, self+0xE8, 0x21), i.e. two 0x34-byte mixing states with pointer tables at +0x34 (0x20 entries, ends at +0xB4) and +0xE8 (0x21 entries, ends at +0x16C) - the exact gap before the next initialised field. Sound_Decoder_DestroyChannels (0x0054B70C) destroys both states via FUN_0012032C. Sound_Decoder_AllocWork (0x0054EF50) carves the 0x1B8-byte block through Sound_WorkBuffer_AllocBlocks (0x00556BA4) and stores it at +0x14. NOTE: the batch offsets 480/496/512/528/544 come from FUN_0054F18C whose self is declared `char *`, so struct_db multiplied its byte offsets by 4 (real offsets +0x78/+0x7C/+0x80/+0x84/+0x88, which are entries of the first block table).

fields.name: maybe_initFlag
fields.evidence: FUN_0054F18C one-shot guard `if (*self == 0) { ...; *self = 1; }`, like 0x00550B00. CAUTION: Sound_Decoder_AllocWork passes the same self as the ring root to Sound_WorkBuffer_AllocBlocks (0x00556BA4), which links free blocks through `*param_1`; byte 0 is therefore either a one-shot flag or the free-block list head depending on which function's object view is meant.

fields.name: maybe_outputMode
fields.evidence: FUN_0054F18C stores 0/1/2 taken from the Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate (0x00518670) result; Sound_Mixer_BuildVolumeMatrix (0x0054C8A4) switches on the same 0..8 output-mode byte.

fields.name: hasWorkArea
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_AllocWork: `if (*(char *)(self + 0x10) == 0) { ...; *(char *)(self + 0x10) = 1; }` - the allocation is done exactly once.

fields.name: blockCount
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_AllocWork stores the Sound_WorkBuffer_AllocBlocks(self, arg2, arg3, 0x1B8) return value here - that helper returns the number of 0x1B8-byte blocks it carved out of the region (0x00556BA4).

fields.name: regionBase
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_AllocWork copies parameter 2 (the byte region that is carved into 0x1B8 blocks) to +0x18; 0x0054F130 passes *(self+0x18) to FUN_00556C04 when the blocks are given back.

fields.name: regionSize
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_AllocWork copies parameter 3 (the region size) to +0x1C; 0x0054F130 passes *(self+0x1C) to FUN_00556C04 on release.

fields.name: mixTableA
fields.evidence: Snd_InitMixingState(self, self+0x34, 0x20) registers this as the first mixing state's block table; FUN_0054F18C later seeds five of its entries (+0x78..+0x88) from the DAT_0054F270 pointer family.

fields.name: mixStateB
fields.evidence: Second SndMixState: Snd_InitMixingState(self+0xB4, self+0xE8, 0x21) initialises it and Sound_Decoder_DestroyChannels calls FUN_0012032C(self+0xB4).

fields.name: mixTableB
fields.evidence: 0x21-entry block table of the second mixing state (Snd_InitMixingState(self+0xB4, self+0xE8, 0x21)); ends at +0x16C where Sound_Decoder_Init starts writing.

fields.name: maybe_mixerIdA
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init clears it to 0 together with the two following words.

fields.name: maybe_mixerIdB
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init clears it to 0 (second of three adjacent mixer words).

fields.name: maybe_mixerIdC
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init clears it to 0 (third of three adjacent mixer words).

fields.name: channelArg2
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init stores parameter 2 at +0x17C next to the >>2 element count.

fields.name: channelCount
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init stores `param_3 >> 2` at +0x180 - a 4-byte element count.

fields.name: maybe_flag184
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init clears it; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_flag188
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init clears it; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_flag18c
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init clears this byte; no reader recovered.

fields.name: isRunning
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_Init sets it to 1, Sound_Decoder_DestroyChannels sets it back to 0.

fields.name: unknown_1e0
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: only FUN_0054F18C touches it and that function's self is `char *`, so struct_db scaled byte +0x78 by 4. The real write is block-table entry +0x78.

fields.name: maybe_decodeMode
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_DecodeFrame (0x0054DD2C) stores parameter 8 at +0x1F0 and branches on `param_8 == 1` to pass a 4-word parameter block to 0x0051846C. (The same batch offset also collects FUN_0054F18C's +0x7C write, scaled by 4.)

fields.name: maybe_formatId
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_DecodeFrame: on the first call it stores `(char)param_9` at +0x1F6 and clears +0x1F7; param_9 is later passed to FUN_00517DE8.

fields.name: maybe_flag1f7
fields.evidence: Sound_Decoder_DecodeFrame clears it on the first call; Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks (0x0054DF60) sets the same byte to 1 when the stream hooks are torn down.

fields.name: unknown_200
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: FUN_0054F18C's byte +0x80 scaled by 4 (a block-table entry).

fields.name: unknown_210
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: FUN_0054F18C's byte +0x84 scaled by 4 (a block-table entry).

fields.name: unknown_220
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: FUN_0054F18C's byte +0x88 scaled by 4 (a block-table entry).

summary: Software voice mixer: two intrusive lists of voice objects (active at +0x04/+0x08, pending at +0x10/+0x14), the per-output gain triple used to build the 4x3 volume matrix, the 3-to-1 output routing mode byte and the free/allocated voice pools.
evidence: Sound_Mixer_TickVoices (0x00550C3C) walks the list at +0x08 and calls 0x0054CBB4/0x0054CFA8/0x0054D4B4 on each entry at node-0x58; Sound_Mixer_BuildVolumeMatrix (0x0054C8A4) builds the 12-float DSP volume matrix from +0x30/+0x34 (per-side pan offsets), +0x44/+0x48/+0x4C (three clamped gains) and the routing byte +0x2D; Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList (0x00550ED0) is the field initialiser.

fields.name: isInitialised
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ShutdownVoices (0x00550E04) tears the lists down and then does `*param_1 = 0` (its self is `char *`, so this is byte 0).

fields.name: pendingListCount
fields.evidence: RelinkVoice (0x00550EA4) calls FUN_0011FCF8(self+0x10, self+0x14, voice+0x58) - an intrusive-list insert whose first two words are the root and its first node.

fields.name: pendingListFirst
fields.evidence: RelinkVoice inserts the voice node at self+0x14; ClearVoiceList (0x0055141C) reads it and destroys the object through vtable slot +0x38 (`(***(code **)(*(int **)(self + 0x14) + 0x38))()`) before clearing the word.

fields.name: maybe_outputChannels
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_BuildVolumeMatrix copies +0x23 into local_3d and passes it to FUN_0054C114, the per-channel matrix helper.

fields.name: maybe_flag27
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList clears this byte; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_dualOutput
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix only applies the +0x30 pan offsets when `*(int *)(self + 8) >= 2 || *(char *)(self + 0x2C) != 1` - a two-output configuration flag.

fields.name: routingMode
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix switches on this byte for cases 1..8 and selects which of the three output columns (local_40/3F/3E) are active.

fields.name: maybe_panOffsetA
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix reads it as float and, in the 2-output path, adds or subtracts a constant depending on the destination side (param_2).

fields.name: maybe_panOffsetB
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix reads it as float in output mode 2: `fVar4 = pfVar2[2] - *(float *)(self + 0x34)`.

fields.name: maybe_activeVoiceCount
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList clears it; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_currentVoiceId
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList writes -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) - a 'no voice' sentinel.

fields.name: maybe_pendingCount
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList clears it; no reader recovered.

fields.name: volumeLeft
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix clamps it between the two DAT_0054CBA4/CBA8 limits, then multiplies output columns 0..3 (the left output) with it.

fields.name: volumeRight
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix clamps it to [DAT_0054CBA8, 0x3F800001] then multiplies output columns 4..7 (the right output).

fields.name: volumeSurround
fields.evidence: BuildVolumeMatrix clamps it the same way and multiplies output columns 8..11 (the surround/rear output).

fields.name: maybe_flag50
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList clears this byte; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_flag51
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList clears this byte; no reader recovered.

fields.name: voiceLock
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ClearVoiceList calls Os_LockSemaphore (0x00117B78) on self+0x70 - the mixer's spin/OS lock word.

fields.name: freeVoiceCount
fields.evidence: ClearVoiceList returns each destroyed voice to this free list with FUN_0011FCBC(self+0x84, node), the intrusive-list push used all over the sound library.

fields.name: freeVoiceFirst
fields.evidence: ClearVoiceList walks `piVar1 = *(int **)(self + 0x88)` while `piVar1 != (int *)(self + 0x88)`: the self-referencing head of the free-voice ring; each node is at voice+0x50.

fields.name: voicePoolRoot
fields.evidence: After destroying a voice, ClearVoiceList calls FUN_00556C38(self+0x90, voice) - the pool return helper (its twin FUN_00556BA4 hands blocks out).

fields.name: maybe_maxVoices
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList writes 3; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_pendingVoiceId
fields.evidence: Sound_Mixer_ResetVoiceList writes -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) - a 'no pending voice' sentinel.

summary: Streamed-voice work block: one 16-entry command ring of 0x44-byte slots at +0x28 (capacity/head/tail/published indices at +0x66/+0x6A/+0x6C/+0x6E), a second 64-entry 8-byte command ring at +0x1848, the async channel/buffer handles and the fade state. Same layout as S_069's Snd_StreamVoice, whose field names are reused here.
evidence: Sound_CommandQueue_Push (0x005EAF40) and PushCommand (0x005EB028) both test bit 0 of byte +0x20, take Os_LockSemaphore, advance `(*(short *)(self + 0x6A) + 1) % 0x10` and write `*(int *)(self + 0x28) + idx * 0x44`; Sound_CommandQueue_Push_2 (0x001EB8C8) uses the 64-entry 8-byte ring at +0x1848 with indices +0x1A48/+0x1A4C. Sound_CommandQueue_Commit (0x005EAEB4) publishes +0x6A into +0x6E.

fields.name: fileHandle
fields.evidence: Read as the stream's async file handle and handed to FUN_0010EFC4/FUN_0010F0C8 (same name as S_069 Snd_StreamVoice+0x18).

fields.name: isActive
fields.evidence: Every public entry tests `*(byte *)(self + 0x20) & 1` and bails out when clear: Commit, Push and PushCommand all start with it.

fields.name: commandSlots
fields.evidence: Pointer to the 16 command slots: `*(int *)(self + 0x28) + *(short *)(self + 0x6A) * 0x44` in Push/PushCommand.

fields.name: currentChannel
fields.evidence: `piVar5 = *(int **)(self + 0x34); ... iVar9 = *piVar5;` then the channel object is started through FUN_0010E438 - same slot as S_069 Snd_StreamVoice+0x34.

fields.name: currentPackChannel
fields.evidence: Read first when the command needs a pack/id pair, exactly like S_069's Snd_StreamVoice+0x44.

fields.name: pendingPackChannel
fields.evidence: Second pack/id holder; written from `piVar5` after a successful bind.

fields.name: bufferIndex
fields.evidence: `piVar5 = (int *)(self + *(int *)(self + 0x50) * 4 + 0x2C)` then `*(int *)(self + 0x50) = (*(int *)(self + 0x50) + 1) % 2` - the double-buffer selector.

fields.name: slotCapacity
fields.evidence: `param_2 < (uint)(int)*(short *)(self + 0x66)` bounds the command index; the ring wraps modulo 0x10.

fields.name: slotWriteIndex
fields.evidence: Advanced by Push: `sVar1 = (short)((*(short *)(self + 0x6A) + 1) % 0x10)` and stored back.

fields.name: slotTailIndex
fields.evidence: Compared with the next write index (`if (*(short *)(self + 0x6C) != sVar1)`) to detect a full ring.

fields.name: slotCommittedIndex
fields.evidence: Commit publishes the write index here: `*(undefined2 *)(self + 0x6E) = *(undefined2 *)(self + 0x6A)`.

fields.name: maybe_streamId
fields.evidence: Read together with the stream handle (S_069 named the same word maybe_streamId).

fields.name: commandSequence
fields.evidence: Incremented for every submitted command and its low byte is copied into the command node (`*(undefined1 *)((int)puVar12 + 1) = *(undefined1 *)(self + 0x1844)`).

fields.name: commandReadIndex
fields.evidence: Ring consumer index of the 64-entry command ring at +0x1848, advanced modulo 0x40 (S_069: commandReadIndex).

fields.name: commandWriteIndex
fields.evidence: Ring producer index, `(index + 1) % 0x40` (S_069: commandWriteIndex).

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: State machine 0/1/4/5/6/8 tested and written in Push_2; S_069 recovered the same byte as Snd_StreamVoice.state.

fields.name: fadeElapsed
fields.evidence: Stored next to the fade target when the voice enters state 5 (S_069: fadeElapsed).

fields.name: fadeTarget
fields.evidence: Second half of the fade pair (S_069: fadeTarget).

summary: Sequence (BRSEQ) event player state: a cursor into the 0x18-byte event table of one sequence, the four 32-bit note-slot masks and the 16-entry {id, note} slot table at +0x3C that the DSP voices are started from.
evidence: Sound_SequencePlayer_ProcessEvents (0x005E9B6C) walks `param_1[1] + i * 0x18` while `i < *(uint *)(*param_1 + 0x10)`, switches on the event type byte at +0xD and starts/stops notes through FUN_001EB8C8 / FUN_001ED940 / FUN_001ED8A4; the note slots are the 8-byte pairs at `self + i*2 + 0xf` (word 0xF..0x1E). Sound_SequencePlayer_Init (0x005E97A4) fills the fields from the sequence resource. The reported size 84 only covers the slot table start; the object really extends to +0xB8.

fields.name: sequenceData
fields.evidence: Init stores parameter 2 here after checking its first word against DAT_005E9820; ProcessEvents reads `*(int *)(*self + 0x10)` (event count) and `*(int *)(*self + 0x14)` (sequence length).

fields.name: eventTable
fields.evidence: Init stores `param_2 + 7` (i.e. resource+0x1C) - the base of the 0x18-byte event records indexed in ProcessEvents.

fields.name: maybe_waitEventTime
fields.evidence: Init/Reset write -1; ProcessEvents stores a between-events timestamp here.

fields.name: maybe_loopEventTime
fields.evidence: Init/Reset write -1; written next to the wait timestamp while skipping events.

fields.name: eventCursor
fields.evidence: Event index: compared with the event count in ProcessEvents and advanced by the number of events consumed.

fields.name: maybe_pendingEventCount
fields.evidence: Init/Reset clear it; no reader recovered.

fields.name: currentNote
fields.evidence: Event type 2 stores the current event pointer here when the note length word at event+0xA is non-zero.

fields.name: currentCommandId
fields.evidence: Event type 1 stores the FUN_001EB8C8 result (a submitted command id) and the owning event pointer.

fields.name: currentEvent
fields.evidence: Second half of the type-1 pair: the event pointer that produced the command.

fields.name: activeNoteCount
fields.evidence: Incremented when a note slot is allocated and decremented when it is freed in ProcessEvents.

fields.name: activeNoteMask
fields.evidence: Set/cleared with `1 << slot` for the 32 note slots; scanned bit by bit when looking for a free slot.

fields.name: pendingNoteCount
fields.evidence: Counted together with pendingNoteMask when a new note has to be queued.

fields.name: pendingNoteMask
fields.evidence: Second slot mask, updated with the same `1 << slot` pattern as activeNoteMask.

fields.name: maybe_releasedNoteCount
fields.evidence: Third count, decremented when a mask bit is cleared in the release path.

fields.name: maybe_releasedNoteMask
fields.evidence: Third 32-bit mask, tested with `1 << slot` in the release path.

fields.name: maybe_noteSlots
fields.evidence: Base of the 16-entry {u32 id, u32 note} slot table (`self + i*2 + 0xf`); FUN_00116AE0(self+0x3C, 0x100) clears its 0x100 bytes in Init/Reset.

fields.name: unknown_40
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: the evidence is `*(uint *)(*param_1 + 0x10)` - the sequence resource's word, not a member of this object.

fields.name: unknown_50
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: the evidence is `*(int *)(*param_1 + 0x14)` - the sequence resource's length word, not a member of this object.

summary: Command node of the sound command list: a 4-byte next pointer, an opcode byte at +0x04, the target object at +0x10 and up to seven arguments, plus the pending-queue node the submit helpers allocate from.
evidence: Sound_Command_ExecuteList (0x00548808) is a `do { switch (opcode) ... } while (param_1 = *(int **)param_1)` loop over `(char)param_1[1]` (opcode at +0x04) that dispatches to the sound API with `param_1[4]` (target object, +0x10) and param_1[5..0xC] as arguments; the submit helpers (0x00549154, 0x00548F90) allocate a node, set its opcode byte and store `self + 0x128` as the node's owner.

fields.name: nextCommand
fields.evidence: Sound_Command_ExecuteList ends every iteration with `param_1 = (int *)*param_1` - a singly linked list of command nodes.

fields.name: opcode
fields.evidence: The dispatch switch reads `(char)param_1[1]`; cases run from 2 to 0x3A.

fields.name: target
fields.evidence: `param_1[4]` is the object every command acts on (vtable calls through `*(int *)param_1[4]`, direct field writes at `param_1[4] + 0x14` etc.).

fields.name: argument0
fields.evidence: First command argument (`param_1[5]`); also read byte-wise at +0x15.

fields.name: argument0High
fields.evidence: `*(undefined1 *)((int)param_1 + 0x15)` - the second byte of argument0, used when an opcode needs a byte parameter.

fields.name: argument1
fields.evidence: Second command argument (`param_1[6]`).

fields.name: argument2
fields.evidence: Third command argument (`param_1[7]`).

fields.name: argument3
fields.evidence: Fourth command argument (`param_1[8]`), also read byte-wise at +0x21.

fields.name: argument3High
fields.evidence: `*(undefined1 *)((int)param_1 + 0x21)` - second byte of argument3.

fields.name: argument4
fields.evidence: Fifth command argument (`param_1[9]`).

fields.name: argument5
fields.evidence: Sixth command argument (`param_1[10]`).

fields.name: maybe_argument7
fields.evidence: Seventh command argument (`param_1[0xC]`); argument6 at +0x2C is not in the batch.

fields.name: maybe_argument14Short
fields.evidence: Opcode 0x2A reads `(short)param_1[0xE]` and passes it to FUN_00552914 - the only command argument that is consumed as 16-bit; the upper half of the word is unused.

fields.name: pendingRing
fields.evidence: Sound_Command_FreeQueued (0x0054B664) drains the local command ring: Os_QueueTryPop(self+0x0B4, ...) then std_RingBuffer_Push(self+0x0B4, node).

fields.name: isPending
fields.evidence: Sound_Command_SubmitTenWords (0x00549154) sets it to 1 after queuing the node.

fields.name: queueNode
fields.evidence: Address stored into every submitted node: `*(int *)(iVar4 + 0x10) = self + 0x128` - the node's back-pointer to this command owner (object ends at +0x12C).

summary: 64-byte player-slot record: an id pair with -1 sentinels, twelve zeroed words and an embedded ring buffer header at +0x3C; cleared by Sound_PlayerSlot_Clear/ResetAll before a new stream is bound to the slot.
evidence: Sound_PlayerSlot_Clear (0x005EA4F0) stores 0 in words 0..14 (with 0xFFFFFFFF in words 2 and 3) and then calls FUN_00116AE0(self+0x0F words, 0x100) which initialises a ring buffer; ResetAll/ClearBusyBit/ClearFlags are damaged Thumb splits (halt_baddata), so no reader of the id words survives. The real object is larger than the reported 64 bytes because the ring at +0x3C needs at least 0x34 more bytes.

fields.name: unknown_04

fields.evidence: Zeroed by Sound_PlayerSlot_Clear; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_ringBuffer
fields.evidence: FUN_00116AE0(self+0x3C, 0x100) initialises an embedded ring buffer here; 0x100 is the element byte count, so the slot record is larger than the reported 64 bytes.

summary: Sound driver object (the same Sound_WorkBuffer layout as Sound_Decoder): the work allocation pair, the profiling sample ring, the deferred-release lists, the release lock and the shutdown flags.
evidence: Sound_Driver_Init (0x0051B7C4) opens the DSP and calls Sound_Driver_Shutdown (0x0051C38C) on failure; maybe_Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling (0x0054D8C0) appends 8-byte timestamps into the array at +0x1B8 when the flag at +0x1F6 is 1; maybe_Sound_Driver_AddDeferredRelease (0x0054DED0) / RemoveDeferredRelease (0x0054DF04) insert and unlink nodes inside the lock at +0x1C4; Sound_Driver_ReleaseAllSeqChannels (0x0054F130) frees the work buffer (+0x18/+0x1C) exactly like Sound_Decoder.

fields.name: isInitialised
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_Driver_ReleaseAllSeqChannels and maybe_Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks both test `*(char *)(self + 0x10) != 0` before releasing and then clear it.

fields.name: workBufferBase
fields.evidence: Passed to FUN_00556C04(self, *(self+0x18), *(self+0x1C)) when the sequence channels are released; Sound_Decoder_AllocWork stores the same pair.

fields.name: workBufferSize
fields.evidence: Second argument of the work-buffer release call FUN_00556C04.

fields.name: profileSamples
fields.evidence: Base of the profiling sample ring: `(*(int *)(self + 0x1B8) + *(int *)(self + 0x1C0) * 8)` receives a {time} pair (two words per sample).

fields.name: profileSampleCapacity
fields.evidence: Bound of the sample ring: `if (*(int *)(self + 0x1C0) < *(int *)(self + 0x1BC))`.

fields.name: profileSampleCount
fields.evidence: Incremented after every stored sample in maybe_Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling.

fields.name: releaseLock
fields.evidence: Os_LockMonitor/Os_UnlockMonitor (FUN_00117E50/FUN_00117ED0) on self+0x1C4 around every deferred-release list operation.

fields.name: maybe_currentReleaseId
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks writes -1 here after draining the lists.

fields.name: deferredListCount
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_Driver_AddDeferredRelease inserts with FUN_0011FCF8(self+0x1D0, self+0x1D4, node+4) - root + first node.

fields.name: deferredListFirst
fields.evidence: Self-referencing head of the deferred-release list (`*(int **)(self + 0x1D4) != (int *)(self + 0x1D4)`), walked by Tick and Shutdown.

fields.name: releaseListFirst
fields.evidence: Second intrusive list, walked by ShutdownHooks and calling `(***(code **)(node[-1] + 0x10))()` on each entry.

fields.name: profileEnabled
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_Driver_TickWithProfiling only samples when this byte equals 1; S_069 recovered the same flag name for Sound_VoicePool.

fields.name: isShutdown
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks and maybe_Sound_Driver_StopTimer set it to 1 when the stream hooks are stopped.

summary: Mixer thread control block: a 64-bit tick accumulator, the display-sync flag, the two callback/argument pairs the loop invokes, the frame monitor and the DSP semaphores.
evidence: Sound_MixerThread_Main (0x00517B6C) is the thread body: it sets the run byte +0x0D, loops while it is non-zero, waits with FUN_00518010 in the non-realtime path or reads the display time with FUN_00517E7C, calls the callback pairs at +0x20/+0x24 and +0x28/+0x2C, runs Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate under the monitor at +0x34, and accumulates the elapsed ticks into the 64-bit value at +0x00/+0x04.

fields.name: tickAccumulatorLow
fields.evidence: Low word of the 64-bit tick sum: `*param_1 = local_30 + elapsed` at the end of Sound_MixerThread_Main.

fields.name: tickAccumulatorHigh
fields.evidence: High word of the same 64-bit tick sum (`param_1[1] = ... + CARRY4(...)`).

fields.name: maybe_frameInterval
fields.evidence: `(char)param_1[2] == 0` selects the blocking wait FUN_00518010 instead of reading the display time; the same byte is later used as a frame-length byte.

fields.name: isRunning
fields.evidence: Set to 1 before the loop and the loop condition is `} while (*(char *)((int)param_1 + 0xd) != 0);`.

fields.name: isSyncToDisplay
fields.evidence: When non-zero the loop queries both display timers through FUN_0051756C and synchronises with FUN_00111D50; zero skips that block.

fields.name: maybe_preCallback
fields.evidence: `if (param_1[8] != 0) { FUN_00117E50(param_1 + 0xd); (*(code *)param_1[8])(param_1[9]); FUN_00117ed0(...); }` - callback guarded by the frame monitor.

fields.name: maybe_preCallbackArg
fields.evidence: Argument passed to maybe_preCallback.

fields.name: maybe_mainCallback
fields.evidence: `if ((char)param_1[0xc] == '\0' && (code *)param_1[10] != 0) (*(code *)param_1[10])(param_1[0xb]);` - main per-frame callback.

fields.name: maybe_mainCallbackArg
fields.evidence: Argument passed to maybe_mainCallback.

fields.name: maybe_pauseFlag
fields.evidence: Low byte of word +0x30; when non-zero the main callback is skipped.

fields.name: frameMonitor
fields.evidence: Os_LockMonitor/Os_UnlockMonitor (FUN_00117E50/FUN_00117ED0) on self+0x34 around Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate and the callbacks.

fields.name: displaySyncSemaphore
fields.evidence: FUN_00111D50(self+0x40) after the two display-time reads - a semaphore release.

fields.name: dspLock

summary: Stream-slot table: a 32-bit live-slot mask at +0xF8, 0x24-byte slot records from +0x110, three counters for in-flight/finishing/queued slots and a 64-entry command ring with indices at +0xA48/+0xA4C.
evidence: Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll (0x00105584) iterates the mask at self+0xF8 bit by bit, addresses the slot record with `self + 0x110 + index * 0x24`, decrements the counters at +0xD4/+0xD8/+0xDC as slots retire and advances the command ring at +0xA48 modulo 0x40. The function is a damaged ARM/Thumb split (unaff_r4/unaff_r8, raw coprocessor accesses), so several operand roles are inferred from the surrounding reads.

fields.name: streamHandle
fields.evidence: Read as the stream's handle and validated (`*(int *)(self + 0x18) != 0`), then passed to FUN_0010EFC4/FUN_0010F0C8 which return the read/write status of that handle.

fields.name: liveSlotCount
fields.evidence: `iVar4 = *(int *)(self + 0xD4); if (0 < iVar4) ...` then decremented whenever a slot's state word becomes 0 (`*(int *)(self + 0xD4) -= 1`).

fields.name: finishingSlotCount
fields.evidence: Decremented on every finished DMA transfer (`*(int *)(self + 0xD8) -= 1`).

fields.name: maybe_queuedSlotCount
fields.evidence: Decremented on the queue-release path (`*(int *)(self + 0xDC) -= 1`).

fields.name: liveSlotMask
fields.evidence: `local_4c = (uint *)(self + 0xF8)` and `*(self + 0xF8) &= ~(1 << slot)` when a slot retires - one bit per slot record.

fields.name: slotRecords
fields.evidence: Base of the slot array: `local_38 = self + 0x110` and the record for slot i is `local_38 + i * 0x24`.

fields.name: commandReadIndex
fields.evidence: Ring consumer index: `*(int *)(self + 0xA48) = (iVar4 + 1) % 0x40`.

fields.name: commandWriteIndex
fields.evidence: Ring producer index compared against commandReadIndex to detect the empty ring.

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: State machine written as 1, 2 and 6 while walking the command ring.

summary: NOT a sound structure: this 0xF7C-byte block is the CTR SDK nn::err fatal-error info record (0xF80 bytes) - a type/result pair, an error-string ring, the detail buffer and the applet launch descriptor. The Sound_ prefix comes from a neighbouring attribution.
evidence: The only recovered function, 0x0051CBF8, is the constructor that established fact 0x0051CBF8..0x0051CD28 lists as building the 0xF80-byte FatalErrInfo: it zeroes +0x00..+0x0A, initialises a ring at +0x0C, sets +0xEE4 = 1, zero-fills 0x89 bytes at +0xEE7 (FUN_001113EC) and writes the -1 timeout at +0xF70; 0x0051CC68 (Err_LaunchFatalErrorApplet) throws it. The batch size 0xF7C is the same record minus its final word.

fields.name: maybe_errorType
fields.evidence: Constructor word 0 is zeroed; nn::err::FatalErrInfo starts with the error type word (established fact: 0x0051CBF8 builds a FatalErrInfo).

fields.name: maybe_resultCode
fields.evidence: Second zeroed word; established fact places the nn::Result at FatalErrInfo+0x04.

fields.name: maybe_isFatal
fields.evidence: Constructor stores 1 at +0xEE4; nn::err uses a 1-byte fatal/abort flag there.

fields.name: unknown_ee5
fields.evidence: Constructor stores 0; no reader recovered.

fields.name: unknown_ee6
fields.evidence: Constructor stores 0; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_messageBuffer
fields.evidence: FUN_001113EC(self+0xEE7, 0x89) zero-fills 0x89 bytes from here - a fixed-size string/detail buffer (only its first byte is listed in the batch).

fields.name: maybe_timeout
fields.evidence: Constructor writes -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) at +0xF70 - an infinite/no-timeout sentinel.

fields.name: unknown_f76
fields.evidence: FUN_006722C4(self+0xF76) initialises an object in the last 10 bytes of the record; purpose unknown.

summary: Per-frame DSP command publisher: a double-buffered set of 24 channel command blocks selected by the frame parity, the frame/sequence counters, the output ring and the 0x260-byte command block copied for the audio thread.
evidence: Sound_Frame_PublishChannelTable (0x00518BE0) reads the sequence counter +0x131E, flips the double-buffer index +0x1320 (`& 1`), pushes the 24 per-channel words at `self + parity*0x60 + i*4 + 0x1174` through FUN_00519DCC, copies 0x260 bytes into self+0x1328 with std_memcpy and increments +0x131E/+0x131D. Sound_Frame_UpdateChannels (0x00518A7C) writes the sequence number through `*(u16 *)(self + parity*4 + 0x109C)` and calls FUN_005171B0 with the frame time.

fields.name: outputRing
fields.evidence: `iVar2 = *(int *)(self + 0x18); ... uVar4 = *(byte *)(iVar2 + 0x10); FUN_0051779C(iVar2, buffer, 0xA0)` - the ring buffer the mixed frames are written to (Sound_RingBuffer per S_069).

fields.name: isPublishing
fields.evidence: Both the update and the publish path bail out unless `*(char *)(self + 0x131C) != 0`.

fields.name: frameCounter
fields.evidence: `*(char *)(self + 0x131D) = *(char *)(self + 0x131D) + 1` on every published frame.

fields.name: sequenceCounter
fields.evidence: `*(short *)(self + 0x131E) = *(short *)(self + 0x131E) + 1`, also used as the double-buffer parity source and with a -1 sentinel.

fields.name: bufferParity
fields.evidence: `*(ushort *)(self + 0x1320) = *(ushort *)(self + 0x131E) & 1`; indexes the 0x60-byte command-block banks and the +0x1304/+0x1314 pointer pairs.

fields.name: previousBufferParity
fields.evidence: `*(ushort *)(self + 0x1322) = *(ushort *)(self + 0x131E) & 1` and then used as `*(u16 *)(self + parity*4 + 0x109C)` - the parity of the frame being published.

fields.name: frameTimestamp
fields.evidence: `iVar8 = *(int *)(self + 0x1324)` is the reference time passed to FUN_005171B0 together with the frame delta.

fields.name: commandBlock
fields.evidence: std_memcpy(self+0x1328, self + parity*4 + 0x1314, 0x260) copies the published DSP command block here; the block is 0x260 bytes, so the reported 4908-byte size only covers its first byte.

summary: Polymorphic stream request/release record (vtable 0x00781D3C): owner back-pointer, active/pending bytes and the intrusive list node used to queue it back to the stream player, with the stream object allocated directly behind it.
evidence: maybe_Sound_Stream_Request_AllocInit (0x00556EC8) stores the vtable DAT_00556EFC, the owner at +0x11C, clears +0x120/+0x121 and then builds the stream at +0x124 through FUN_005506AC, returning `result - 0x124`; Cancel (0x00549288) and CancelB (0x00556E68) check the +0x120 byte, unlink the node at +0xF8 from owner+8/owner+0x14 and call vtable slot +0x10.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: AllocInit stores DAT_00556EFC at offset 0; the resolved vtable 0x00781D3C has two slots (0x006633E0 and 0x00556F00).

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlotPhantom
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: the only evidence is `(***(code **)(*param_1 + 0x10))(param_1)` - a virtual call through vtable slot 4 (byte +0x10), not a field at +0x40.

fields.name: maybe_queueNode
fields.evidence: The intrusive list node: Cancel does `FUN_0011fcbc(owner + 8, self + 0x3E words)` and `FUN_0011fcf8(owner + 0x14, owner + 0x18, self + 0x3E words)`, i.e. the node lives at byte +0xF8 and links into the owner's free list.

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: AllocInit stores parameter 2 at +0x11C; Cancel reads it back as the list owner (`iVar1 = param_1[0x47]`).

fields.name: isActive
fields.evidence: Cancel/CancelB only run when `(char)param_1[0x48] != '\0'` and clear it first; AllocInit clears it.

fields.name: maybe_isPending
fields.evidence: Cleared by AllocInit and by both cancel paths next to isActive; purpose unknown.

fields.name: maybe_embeddedStream
fields.evidence: FUN_005506AC(self+0x124) initialises an object whose fields reach +0xC0; AllocInit returns `result - 0x124`, so the request and its stream share one allocation and this word is the stream's first member.

summary: ADPCM channel table: a one-shot constructor that links every 0x60-byte ADPCM channel into an intrusive list and stores the resulting channel count; the batch offsets for this class are 4x the real byte offsets (see evidence).
evidence: Sound_AdpcmChannel_InitTable (0x00550B00) computes `count = (bytes * DAT_00550B74) >> 0x26` (a divide by 0x60), then for each channel calls FUN_0011FCF8(self+0x10, self+0x14, channel+0x58) and stores the count at +0x1C and +0x20 before setting the isInitialised byte. The function declares `char *param_1`, so the listed offsets 64/80/112/128 are 4x the real +0x10/+0x14/+0x1C/+0x20.

fields.name: isInitialised
fields.evidence: `if (*param_1 == '\0') { ...; *param_1 = '\x01'; }` - one-shot table build.

fields.name: maybe_channelListRoot
fields.evidence: REAL OFFSET +0x10: FUN_0011FCF8(self+0x10, self+0x14, channel+0x58) - the root of the intrusive list of 0x60-byte ADCMP channels.

fields.name: maybe_channelListFirst
fields.evidence: REAL OFFSET +0x14: the first node of that list (each node is at channel+0x58).

fields.name: maybe_channelCount
fields.evidence: REAL OFFSET +0x1C: `*(uint *)(self + 0x1C) = count` where count = bytes / 0x60.

fields.name: maybe_channelCapacity
fields.evidence: REAL OFFSET +0x20: receives the same count as +0x1C; either a duplicate capacity or the total byte size divided by the entry size.

summary: Sequence-resource header: five relative offsets to the tagged sub-record blocks (types 2..6) that Sound_SeqResource_ResolveId indexes when a sequence id is looked up.
evidence: Sound_SeqResource_ResolveId (0x0065F87C) switches on the top byte of the id and, for each type, does `puVar1 = (uint *)(self + *(int *)(self + OFF))` where OFF is +0xC (type 2), +0x14 (type 3), +0x1C (type 5), +0x24 (type 6) and +0x2C (type 4); the block starts with a count followed by {offset, id} pairs (stride 8) resolved through 0x00661534.

fields.name: blockOffsetType2
fields.evidence: Case 2 of ResolveId: `puVar1 = (uint *)(self + *(int *)(self + 0xC))` then a bounds check and `puVar1[id * 2 + 2]` field lookup.

fields.name: blockOffsetType3
fields.evidence: Case 3: block located through `*(int *)(self + 0x14)`.

fields.name: blockOffsetType5
fields.evidence: Case 5: block located through `*(int *)(self + 0x1C)`.

fields.name: blockOffsetType6
fields.evidence: Case 6: block located through `*(int *)(self + 0x24)`.

fields.name: blockOffsetType4
fields.evidence: Case 4: block located through `*(int *)(self + 0x2C)` (the switch orders the cases 4 and 5 differently from the offsets).

summary: Small stream-request record: the request value, its intrusive list links and the stream object plus generation it belongs to; released by marking the stream complete.
evidence: maybe_Sound_StreamRequest_Release (0x001D0780) stores parameter 2 at +0, checks `*(int *)(self + 0x18) == *(int *)(stream + 0xC)` (generation match), calls FUN_0055DA70 and unlinks +0x08/+0x0C from the owner list; maybe_Sound_StreamRequest_MarkComplete (0x001D0720) sets the stream's +0x284 byte.

fields.name: requestValue
fields.evidence: Release stores parameter 2 here: `*param_1 = param_2`.

fields.name: nextNode
fields.evidence: Unlink writes `*(int *)(nextNode + 4) = prevNode` - this word is the node that the list's +4 back link points at.

fields.name: prevNode
fields.evidence: Unlink writes `*(int *)(prevNode + 8) = nextNode` - the node's +8 back link.

fields.name: stream
fields.evidence: `iVar2 = *(int *)(self + 0x14)`; MarkComplete sets `*(undefined1 *)(*(int *)(self + 0x14) + 0x284) = 1`.

fields.name: streamGeneration
fields.evidence: Compared with the stream's +0xC generation counter before the release is applied.
